subject.title: fix(providers): publish Meta under canonical package name

question: Should the current-main-only Meta provider be renamed to `meta` and published as `@openclaw/meta-provider` for the next release train?
rationale: The patch is coherent and fixes the active publication gap, but it changes provider ids, auth setup, package publication, shrinkwrap, official catalogs, and release notes, which are maintainer-owned release/compatibility surfaces.

options.title: Confirm and land the canonical package rename
options.body: Merge after release-owner confirmation that `meta`, `@openclaw/meta-provider`, `MODEL_API_KEY`, the shrinkwrap, and the changelog entry are the intended 2026.6.11 release shape.

options.title: Keep bundled-only for now
options.body: Remove the npm/ClawHub publication metadata and keep the provider bundled until a later package release decision is made.

options.title: Pause before release
options.body: Leave the PR open while maintainers decide whether Meta should publish as an official external install route or remain only in core.

recommendation.title: Confirm and land the canonical package rename
recommendation.body: Merge after release-owner confirmation that `meta`, `@openclaw/meta-provider`, `MODEL_API_KEY`, the shrinkwrap, and the changelog entry are the intended 2026.6.11 release shape.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned to the live PR and is the trusted actor on the dependency-guarded current head.
